help.subtitel: Welcome to your tactical dashboard. Follow the guidelines below to effectively manage artillery operations, analyze enemy threats, and execute fire missions with precision.
help.pCampText: The green tent icon on the map is your base. Be careful not to shoot it. If you accidentally hit and destroy your own base, the game is over.
help.pEnemyText: Enemies are shown as white icons on the map. You need to find their location and shoot them to get points.
help.pChatboxText: This box shows messages from the system, including enemy locations and game events.
help.pChatboxsendText: You can type commands here to interact with the game. If you need firing coordinates, simply type the grid sector (e.g., 'Target C5'). The Radio Operator will calculate the exact Degree and Mil settings for you.
help.pControlpanelfullText: This area contains the main controls for aiming and firing your weapon in the game.
help.pControlweaponText: Use the Degree slider to rotate the weapon left or right. Use the Mil slider to adjust the vertical angle to shoot further away.
help.pRoundandfireText: Choose your ammo type here. HE Shell does more damage in a small area, while Shrapnel covers a larger area with less damage. Click the FIRE button to shoot.
help.pDegreeaimText: The map is divided into a grid. You can use these grid lines to estimate the distance and location of the targets.
help.pDebugsettingText: These options help you test the game. You can turn on a visible aim line, show hitboxes around objects, or restart the game.
help.pTablefireText: This table shows you what Mil value to set on the slider based on how far away the target is in meters.
help.pEnemylistText: This table displays information about different enemy types, including their health points, size, and the score you get for destroying them.
help.pKeyboardText: Use W/S or Up/Down arrows to adjust Mil. Use A/D or Left/Right arrows to adjust Degree. Press Spacebar to Fire.
help.pKeywordsText:
You can use these keywords in the chat box to issue commands or request intel:

Acknowledge: copy that, roger, affirmative, confirmed, understood, yes, ok, yep
Repeat: call again, repeat, say again, what, did not copy, unreadable
Help: help, assist, guide, tutorial, instructions, sos, mayday
Friendly Loc: your location, friendly loc, base pos, report pos, grid friendly
Enemy Spot: enemy spot, targets, hostiles, contacts
Status: sitrep, status, base hp, damage report, update, condition
Ammo: ammo, shell, round, he, high explosive, shrapnel, frag, payload
Aiming: help aim, firing solution, fire table, azimuth, elevation, mil, degree, coordinates
Praise: good job, gj, thanks, nice hit, bullseye, target destroyed, splash, gg, wp
Panic: oh no, we are dying, panic, overrun, swarmed, surrounded, pinned down, broken arrow
Fire Command: fire, shoot, open fire, fire for effect, send it, engage, weapons free, light em up, rain hell, strike
Discipline: Using profanity or insults will trigger a radio discipline warning.


Targeting Grid: Type any grid coordinate (e.g., C5, target B12) and the operator will calculate the exact Degree and Mil settings to hit that location.

about.subtitel: Declassified information regarding the development and technology behind Artillery Command.
about.subtitleProjectCard:
Artillery Command is a tactical simulation game focused on coordination, precision, and strategic resource management. Players act as fire support commanders, calculating trajectories via grid coordinates and managing radio communications to destroy enemy targets.

Inspired by the realistic mechanics of military simulators like Arma and Squad, the game shifts focus from frontline combat to the behind-the-scenes challenges of indirect fire support emphasizing map reading, communication protocols, and analytical skills.

Ultimately, it synchronizes mathematical logic with an interactive digital environment to deliver a challenging and deeply immersive tactical experience.
